title: Why High-rank Neural Networks Generalize?: An Algebraic Framework with RKHSs
claim: Prior bounds apply only to restrictive model classes; ours builds an RKHS on a larger function space, covering realistic models.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, colored outcome boxes at right
description: Two horizontal rows labeled "Existing" and "Ours" compare how each Koopman-based bound is built. Each row is a left-to-right chain of white text boxes joined by arrows. The first box gives the model assumption: smooth, unbounded activations in the existing row, and a wider class of activations (Leaky ReLU, sigmoid, tanh) in the ours row. The second box names the function space: a Sobolev space (RKHS) in the existing row, and an RKHS on the parameter space built from L² in the ours row. The third box is the same in both rows: Koopman operator and reproducing property. A small gray oval between the rows reads "Sobolev ⊂ L²". The last box in each row is rounded and colored. It is blue in the existing row and lists limits (only unrealistic models, hard to evaluate factors). It is peach in the ours row and lists benefits (realistic models, easy to evaluate factors). The eye goes first to the row labels and the colored end boxes.
caption: Summary of the framework of the existing and proposed Koopman-based bounds
abstract: We derive a new Rademacher complexity bound for deep neural networks using Koopman operators, group representations, and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). The proposed bound describes why the models with high-rank weight matrices generalize well. Although there are existing bounds that attempt to describe this phenomenon, these existing bounds can be applied to limited types of models. We introduce an algebraic representation of neural networks and a kernel function to construct an RKHS to derive a bound for a wider range of realistic models. This work paves the way for the Koopman-based theory for Rademacher complexity bounds to be valid for more practical situations.
